key_insight: Detonation-sprayed Fe-based amorphous coatings achieve better corrosion and wear performance when droplet flattening is high and porosity is low, with humidity strongly influencing tribological behavior.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing spray parameters to maximize disk-like splat formation and minimize pores can improve long-term protection of carbon-steel components in humid service environments.
method: Prepared Fe-based amorphous coatings on Q235 carbon steel by detonation spray under different spraying parameters.
Compared coating microstructure, long-term corrosion behavior, and wear behavior across humidity conditions.
Evaluated droplet morphology, porosity, friction coefficient, and wear rate.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that coatings with higher droplet circularity/expansion formed denser fine-lamellar structures, while increasing humidity reduced friction coefficient and wear rate, and higher porosity correlated with poorer corrosion resistance.
watch_item: Performance depends strongly on spray parameter control and environmental humidity, so results may not transfer directly without matching processing and service conditions.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
